title: Private deployments: VPC & on-prem comprehensive deployment + Day-2 ops
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary and purpose:

This document is the canonical Redwood reference for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates: reference architectures, packaging and artifact guidance, step-by-step deployment procedures, Day-2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backups), and upgrade & rollback procedures. It is intended for Solutions Engineering, Platform SREs, and Customer Site Reliability Engineers working on customer private installations.

Scope:
- Supported deployment modes: VPC (cloud-hosted private control plane + customer VPC peering), fully on-prem air-gapped installs, and hybrid edge (control plane in Redwood, data plane in customer VPC).
- Components covered: control-plane, redwood-operator, model-worker, agent, private-proxy, kv-cache, observability exporter, kms-integration.
- Not covered: non-production PoC single-node installs (see separate quickstart).

Key goals:
- Repeatable, auditable deployment steps with ownership and rollback paths.
- Clear Day-2 runbook items: logging, alerting, capacity changes, security patching.
- Minimum customer requirements and gating checks to accelerate onboarding.

Reference architectures (high level):

1) VPC deployment (recommended for cloud customers)
- Control plane: Redwood-managed, multi-region, TLS authenticated.
- Data plane: Customer-managed VPC with NAT/egress rules, subnets for worker pools, and load-balancers for ingress.
- Networking: AWS VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink (preferred for cross-account), with CIDR white-listing.
- Typical service layout:
  - Private-proxy (N LB) -> Gateway subnets -> Worker subnets (model-worker pods on GPU instances)
  - KV cache Redis cluster in private subnet (replicated)
  - KMS integration via customer KMS endpoint (optional)

2) On-prem air-gapped deployment
- All control and data plane components run inside customer network behind a firewall.
- Packaging: OCI bundle delivered via tarball or private registry mirror.
- Update channel: offline .tgz packages + SHA256 signed manifests.
- Required infra: Kubernetes (1.24+), GPU device plugin (NVIDIA or ROCm), an internal registry, and an internal time/NTP service.

3) Hybrid edge deployment
- Control plane in Redwood for management & telemetry; model inference stays in customer VPC.
- Control traffic limited to management API endpoints over mTLS.

Packaging and artifacts:
- Artifacts produced by builds/release pipeline:
  - Helm chart: redwood-private-chart v{version}.tgz
  - OCI images: registry.redwood-inference/private/{component}:{tag}
  - Offline bundle: redwood-private-bundle-{version}.tgz (includes Helm chart, CRDs, YAML templates, and SHA256 manifest)

Pre-deployment requirements (customer & Redwood checklist):
| Area | Minimum requirement | Responsible |
|---|---|---|
| Kubernetes | 1.24+ control plane; 100Gi free PVC for logs | Customer |
| GPUs | NVIDIA drivers 525.x or ROCm 5.x; nvidia-device-plugin installed | Customer |
| Network | CIDR ranges, NAT/egress, required ports (see below) | Customer/RE |
| Registry | Private container registry with pull credentials OR access to Redwood private registry | Customer |
| Identity & Keys | KMS endpoint OR provide customer-managed HSM certs | Customer |
| Access | Bastion + VPN for SRE access; least-privilege IAM roles for cloud | Customer/SE |

Required ports (minimum):
- 443 (HTTPS) outbound for optional telemetry/control-plane reachability (VPC hybrid).
- 2379-2380 (etcd) internal for multi-node etcd clusters (on-prem only).
- 10250 (kubelet), 30000-32767 (NodePort range) as defined by Helm values.

Deployment checklist (high level):
1. Validate prerequisites and obtain customer access (console, kubeconfig, registry creds).
2. Confirm network topology and CIDR allocations; open required ports in firewall rules.
3. Upload artifacts to customer registry (on-prem) or ensure pull access to Redwood registry.
4. Install CRDs and namespace scaffolding.
5. Deploy core control plane components: redwood-operator, private-proxy, observability exporters.
6. Deploy model-worker pools and attach GPUs.
7. Run smoke tests and performance sanity checks (see Test & Verification section).

Step-by-step VPC deployment (example commands):
1) Prepare values.yaml (example snippet):

# values.yaml (snippet)
controlPlane:
  mode: "private"
  endpoint: "https://control.redwood-inference.internal"
  tls: true
registry:
  url: "registry.customer.internal"
  credentialsSecret: "registry-creds"
modelWorker:
  replicas: 3
  gpu:
    type: "nvidia-a10"
    driverVersion: "525.60"

2) Install CRDs and apply namespace:
$ kubectl apply -f crds/
$ kubectl create ns redwood-private

3) Install Helm chart:
$ helm install redwood-private redwood-private-chart-1.14.0.tgz -n redwood-private -f values.yaml

4) Verify pods and GPU mounts:
$ kubectl -n redwood-private get pods
$ kubectl -n redwood-private describe pod redwood-model-worker-0 | grep -i nvidia

Test & verification (smoke tests):
- healthcheck endpoint: GET /healthz (should return 200 and component statuses).
- model inference test: run sample request against private-proxy and validate tokens/sec and latency (reference CLI):
$ redwoodctl infer --endpoint https://private-proxy.customer --model redwood-small --prompt "Hello" --timeout 10s
- KV cache consistency: run redis-cli INFO replication and check role: master/replica.

Day-2 operations (operational runbook):
Observability and alerts:
- Metrics exported to Prometheus: cpu_usage, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), error_rate.
- Recommended alerts and thresholds:
  - model-worker GPU_utilization < 15% for > 30m (scale down candidate)
  - request_latency_p95 > 400ms for 5m (page oncall)
  - error_rate > 1% for 10m (investigate regressions)
- Logs: centralize application logs to the customer ELK/Datadog; include structured fields: request_id, model, route, user_tenant.

Capacity changes and scaling:
- Scale up model-worker Pool: update Helm values modelWorker.replicas or use K8s HPA configured with custom GPU-aware metrics adapter.
- Recommended scale step: +20% of baseline for initial ramp; run load test (locust/bench) before opening traffic.

Backups and persistence:
- Etcd & Redis backups: daily snapshot to S3-compatible storage (or NAS snapshot) with 14-day retention.
- Model artifacts: immutable registry; retain at least 3 recent model versions.

Security patching and maintenance windows:
- Monthly security window: schedule node OS updates and driver updates in staggered rolling manner (50% at a time).
- GPU driver updates require drain+reboot sequence with graceful draining of KV cache and model-worker state.

Upgrade & rollback procedures:
Upgrade strategy options:
- Canary rolling upgrade (recommended): deploy new control plane & worker images to a small canary subset (10% of capacity), run synthetic validation, then progressive rollout.
- Blue/Green (for critical customers): provision parallel namespace redwood-private-v2, validate, switch ingress routing.

Canary upgrade steps (example):
1) Prepare new Helm chart and tag images (vX.Y.Z).
2) Update Helm values to create canary workerPool: replicas: 1 (or 10% capacity) and apply:
$ helm upgrade redwood-private -n redwood-private -f values-canary.yaml redwood-private-chart-vX.Y.Z.tgz
3) Run canary validation (10m):
  - healthcheck, smoke inference tests, perf tests at 25% load of normal traffic.
4) If validations pass, incrementally increase replica count in 10% steps with 10-20 minute observation windows.
5) If failure detected, execute rollback (see below).

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- Helm rollback to previous release:
$ helm rollback redwood-private <REVISION> -n redwood-private
- If rollback fails or DB migration is irreversible: follow emergency rollback runbook and open incident with SE & SRE.

Emergency rollback checklist:
1) Quiesce incoming traffic (update load-balancer to drain).
2) Scale worker pools to previous stable revision using Helm or kubectl.
3) Restore redis snapshot if KV corruption is suspected.
4) Rotate keys/certs if credentials were part of the failing release.

Customer requirements library (common customer asks and recommended minimums):
- Network: allow egress to Redwood artifact endpoints (unless using offline bundle). Provide CIDR and gateway IPs in onboarding form.
- Identity: support for OIDC + RBAC or SAML; provide one service account for SRE with time-limited access.
- Encryption: TLS for all internal components; optional HSM for KMS-managed keys.
- Compliance: retain audit logs for 90 days (customer may request longer).
- Capacity planning: 1 A10 GPU serves ~12 concurrent small-generation sessions (p95 latency < 200ms); use this as initial capacity planning metric.

Runbook ownership and escalation:
- Primary oncall: customer SRE (first responder).
- Secondary: Redwood Platform SRE (pager duty: redwood-platform).
- Escalation timeline: 15m initial response, 60m deep-dive, 4h executive notification for Sev2+.

Appendix A — Example Terraform snippet (VPC peering):
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "redwood_customer" {
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id = var.redwood_vpc_id
  peer_region = var.redwood_region
  tags = { Name = "redwood-customer-peering" }
}

Appendix B — Helm values example (full snippet):
replicaCount: 3
modelWorker:
  replicas: 3
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  image:
    repository: registry.customer.internal/redwood/model-worker
    tag: v1.14.0

Appendix C — SLOs (recommended):
| Metric | Target |
|---|---|
| Availability (control-plane) | 99.95% monthly |
| Inference latency (small models) p95 | <= 200ms |
| Inference success rate | >= 99.5% |
